parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/user/user.entity.ts is declared as domain. The class doesn't model a pure domain concept. It also defines how the data is stored: the @Entity('user'), @PrimaryGeneratedColumn, @Column, @ManyToMany/@JoinTable and @OneToMany decorators set the table, columns and join tables, which is persistence (infrastructure) work. The @BeforeInsert hashPassword() hook uses argon2 to hash the password inside an ORM insert event, so the domain object is tied to the database write cycle and to a specific hashing library, which is also infrastructure work. The @IsEmail() decorator from class-validator is input validation of the kind used for DTOs and request pipes, which belongs to the application or presentation layer. Because the file carries persistence and framework responsibilities in a domain-layer unit, it fails the rubric.

violations.message: UserEntity carries TypeORM persistence mapping (@Entity('user'), @PrimaryGeneratedColumn, @Column, @ManyToMany/@JoinTable, @OneToMany). That is infrastructure-layer persistence work inside a domain-layer file.

hashPassword() is an ORM @BeforeInsert lifecycle hook that calls argon2.hash. Tying password hashing to the database insert event and to a specific crypto library is infrastructure work, not domain work.
@IsEmail() from class-validator on the email field is framework input validation. It belongs in an application/presentation DTO, not in the domain entity.
